targets.authors: Hurst, J. E., & Kavanagh, P. S.
targets.title: Life history strategies and psychopathology: The faster the life strategies, the more symptoms of psychopathology.
targets.evidence_quote:
This reproduction tests the claim from Hurst & Kavanagh (2017) that individuals with faster
life strategies report more symptoms of psychopathology.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
The reproduction attempt relied on the dataset from the original study with data from N =
138 individuals. We found a significant correlation between life history (i.e., Mini-K total life
history score) and psychopathology (i.e., index of psychopathology) with age as a covaria-
 te, r = -.513, p < .001. The correlation was in the same direction of that in the original stu-
dy, with faster life strategies associated with more symptoms of psychopathology, and the
focal variable p value and the focal variable coefficient value were the same as in the ori-
ginal study. Thus, this reproduction of the claim was successful according to the SCORE
criteria.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
The statistical analysis is the same as in the original study. A partial correlation analysis is
conducted between life history (i.e., Mini-K total life history score) and psychopathology
(i.e., index of psychopathology) with age as a covariate.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Original-data partial correlation reproduced the focal coefficient and p-value; report uses the same analysis with no alternative specifications.
